text: When are the CMA Awards 2026? Date, time, channel and host. The 60th annual CMA Awards are Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, starting at 7 p.m. Central (8 p.m. Eastern). The show airs live on ABC and streams on Disney+, and it is available on Hulu the next day. Lainey Wilson hosts for the third year in a row.. The 60th annual CMA Awards air live from Nashville on Nov. 18, 2026, with Ella Langley leading the nominations.. The Country Music Association Awards, often shortened to the CMAs, mark their 60th edition this year. Ella Langley leads the nominations with nine, including for "Choosin' Texas," with her mentor Miranda Lambert close behind. Ben West and Kacey Musgraves have five nominations each, and Cody Johnson, Chris Stapleton and Stephen Wilson Jr. Have four each. The Entertainer of the Year nominees are Luke Combs, Cody Johnson, Ella Langley, Chris Stapleton and Lainey Wilson, who is seeking a repeat win. The New Artist of the Year nominees are Avery Anna, Carter Faith, Emily Ann Roberts, Tucker Wetmore and Stephen Wilson Jr. Winners are chosen by voting members of the Country Music Association, which is made up of people who work in the country music industry.

Has a defense secretary ever been impeached? What history shows. No. No U.S. Secretary of defense has ever been impeached. The closest case is William Belknap, President Ulysses S. Grant's secretary of war, whom the House impeached on March 2, 1876, minutes after he resigned. The only other Cabinet member ever impeached is Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas, in 2024.. Rep. Thomas Massie forced a House vote this week on eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.. Belknap faced five articles of impeachment over a kickback scheme tied to a military trading post. According to the U.S. Senate, he resigned to Grant at the White House just minutes before the House voted unanimously to impeach him. At his Senate trial, a majority voted against him on all five articles, but none reached the two-thirds needed to convict, and he was acquitted on Aug. 1, 1876. Many senators who voted not guilty doubted the Senate had jurisdiction over a former official. Mayorkas became the first sitting Cabinet secretary to be impeached when the House voted 214-213 on Feb. 13, 2024, over his handling of the southern border. On April 17, 2024, the Senate voted that both articles were unconstitutional, ending the trial without a verdict on the charges. On Nov. 9, 2026, Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., filed a privileged resolution with eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, starting a two-legislative-day clock that requires House leaders to act by Wednesday, Nov. 11. Hegseth called them "sham articles of impeachment." Leaders could move to table the resolution, which would kill it without a vote on the charges. Impeachment needs a simple majority in the House; removal needs a two-thirds vote in the Senate.

Is Thomas Massie a Republican or Democrat? His party, explained. Thomas Massie is a Republican. He has represented Kentucky's 4th Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2012. He lost the Republican primary on May 19, 2026, to Trump-endorsed Ed Gallrein, so his current term ends when the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3, 2027.. Massie, a Kentucky Republican leaving Congress in January, forced a House vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Nov. 9, 2026.. Massie has often broken with President Donald Trump. He pushed for the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files, criticized the war in Iran and voted against the president's signature tax legislation in 2025. Trump handpicked and endorsed Gallrein, a former Navy SEAL, and said after the primary that Massie "deserves to lose." Gallrein went on to defeat Democrat Melissa Strange for the seat in the Nov. 3, 2026, general election. On Nov. 9, 2026, Massie filed a privileged resolution with eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Under House rules, leaders must bring the measure up by Wednesday, Nov. 11, although they could move to table it.

What is the difference between the Latin Grammys and the Grammys?. The Latin Grammys are a separate awards show run by the Latin Recording Academy for music performed mainly in Spanish or Portuguese, from Latin America, Spain, Portugal and Latino communities in the U.S. And Canada. The Grammys are run by the Recording Academy. The 27th Latin Grammys air Nov. 12, 2026, from Las Vegas.. The 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards take place Nov. 12, 2026, at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas.. The Recording Academy, which presents the Grammys, formed the Latin Recording Academy in 1997, and the first Latin Grammy ceremony was held on Sept. 13, 2000, at the Staples Center in Los Angeles. Organizers said the "Latin music universe was deemed too large to fit on the Grammy Awards." Winners are chosen by a peer vote of the Latin academy's members, who live in the U.S., Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula. To qualify, a recording must be at least 60% in Spanish or Portuguese (the threshold was 51% before 2024) and be released in North, Central or South America, the Caribbean, Spain or Portugal. Recordings in other Ibero-American languages, such as Catalan, Basque, Galician, Quechua and Guarani, can be accepted by a majority vote. The eligibility year runs from June 1 to May 30. Like the Grammys, the show has four genre-free general categories: Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year and Best New Artist. The 2026 ceremony, sometimes stylized "Latin GRAMMYs," takes place at the MGM Grand Garden Arena on Thursday, Nov. 12. The broadcast starts at 8 p.m. ET on Univision, UniMás, Galavisión and ViX, with Roselyn Sánchez hosting for the 10th time. Edgar Barrera leads with 10 nominations, and Karol G, Rosalía, Jorge Drexler and Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso have seven each.

When do Medicaid work requirements start? Jan. 1, 2027, in most states. Under the 2025 federal budget law, states must begin Medicaid work requirements for adults in the Affordable Care Act expansion group by Jan. 1, 2027. A few states are earlier: Nebraska started May 1, 2026, Montana planned July 1, 2026, and Iowa plans Dec. 1, 2026. States showing a good-faith effort can get more time, until Dec. 31, 2028, at the latest.. With less than two months left before the Jan. 1, 2027, federal deadline, states are preparing to enforce the new Medicaid work rules, and Iowa plans to start Dec. 1, 2026.. The rule covers expansion adults through age 64. To keep coverage, they must log 80 hours a month of work, community service or a work program, or qualify for an exemption, according to KFF. Mandatory exemptions include parents and caretakers of children 13 and under, people who are medically frail, and people who are pregnant or postpartum. States may also grant short-term hardship exceptions. States check compliance when someone applies, looking back at least one month and up to three months, and again at renewal, which for this group happens every six months. Arkansas began a "soft" launch on July 1, 2026, with no one losing coverage before Jan. 1, 2027. Georgia, the only state with an operating work-requirement waiver, has a waiver that expires Dec. 31, 2026. The Congressional Budget Office projected $326 billion in federal Medicaid savings over 10 years, mainly from people losing coverage.

When are the National Book Awards 2026? Date, host and finalists. The winners of the 77th National Book Awards will be announced on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 8 p.m. Eastern, at a ceremony at Cipriani Wall Street in New York. Actor Kyle MacLachlan hosts, and the event is livestreamed free at nationalbook.org and on the National Book Foundation's YouTube channel.. The National Book Foundation names the 2026 National Book Award winners at a ceremony in New York on Nov. 18, 2026.. Awards are given in five categories: Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature and Young People's Literature. Each winner receives $10,000, a bronze medal and a statue, and each finalist receives $1,000 and a bronze medal. Michelle Zauner is the musical guest. The fiction finalists are Hannah Lillith Assadi's "Paradiso 17," Edwidge Danticat's "Dèy," Julián Delgado Lopera's "Pretend You're Dead and I Carry You," Valeria Luiselli's "Beginning Middle End" and Morgan Thomas's "Mad Eden." The translated literature finalists include Karl Ove Knausgaard's "The School of Night," translated by Martin Aitken. The Young People's Literature finalists are Elana K. Arnold's "Holloway," Tae Keller's "When Tomorrow Burns," Keala Kendall's "That Which Feeds Us: A Hawaiian Gothic," David Levithan and Gabriel Duckels's "The Fight of Our Lives: AIDS in America" and Julian Randall's "Shook." The poetry finalists include Victoria Chang's "Tree of Knowledge" and Brenda Hillman's "Still House in the Desert."

Is there a planet alignment in November 2026? What to see at dawn. Yes, in the morning sky. Around Nov. 12, 2026, Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter line up before sunrise, and Mars passes about one degree from Jupiter on Nov. 14-17. Venus and Mercury sit low in the southeast, and Mercury is best around Nov. 20. The planets only look close together from Earth; they are not physically near each other.. Four planets line up in the predawn sky in mid-November 2026, with a close Mars-Jupiter conjunction on Nov. 14-17.. Popular Science says the four planets form a line before dawn around Nov. 12: Venus in the southeast, Mars high in the east, Jupiter lower in the east and Mercury low in the southeast just before sunrise. The three bigger planets stay roughly in line all month. The highlight is the pairing of Mars and Jupiter. BBC Sky at Night Magazine says Mars passes around a degree north of Jupiter, with closest approach on Nov. 14-17. Jupiter, at about magnitude -2.0, will look far brighter than reddish Mars, at about +0.7. Popular Science lists Nov. 16 as the conjunction date, with the bright star Regulus nearby. No telescope is needed, but do not point binoculars toward the horizon once the sun is up. Mercury reaches its greatest western elongation, its best morning position, on Nov. 20, with brilliant Venus just above it. The Leonid meteor shower is predicted to peak on Nov. 18, usually at 10 to 15 meteors an hour, and the Full Beaver Moon on Nov. 24 is the first of three supermoons in a row.

Is The Empress on Netflix a true story? The real Sisi, explained. Yes, mostly. Netflix's The Empress (German title: Die Kaiserin) is based on the real life of Empress Elisabeth of Austria, known as Sisi, and her marriage to Emperor Franz Joseph I, but it invents and rearranges many scenes. The third and final season arrives on Netflix on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026.. The third and final season of Netflix's German period drama The Empress premieres Nov. 12, 2026.. The real Elisabeth was born on Dec. 24, 1837, in Munich and married Franz Joseph on April 24, 1854, in Vienna. The German series, created by Katharina Eyssen, stars Devrim Lingnau as Elisabeth and Philip Froissant as Franz Joseph. Season 1 premiered on Sept. 29, 2022, and Season 2 on Nov. 22, 2024. According to Netflix, Season 3 opens after the Sardinian War, with Franz Joseph returning traumatized. Elisabeth leaves Vienna to recover on a distant island and meets Hungarian leader Count Andrássy, while Franz Joseph's brother Maximilian heads to Mexico to take a throne. Those threads are rooted in history: in October 1860 a lung specialist advised Elisabeth to stay on Madeira; Gyula Andrássy, whom she backed, became Hungary's first prime minister after the 1867 compromise; and she was crowned Queen of Hungary on June 8, 1867. Maximilian became Emperor of Mexico on April 10, 1864, and was executed in Querétaro on June 19, 1867. The show takes liberties. There is no evidence that Maximilian conspired against his brother, as the series depicts. In real life, Elisabeth first met Franz Joseph indoors over tea in Bad Ischl with relatives present, and he did not propose in public. Franz Joseph's brother Karl Ludwig, who was in love with Elisabeth, does not appear at all.

What is a hip pointer injury? Football's painful hip bruise. A hip pointer is a bruise, or contusion, on the upper outer part of the hip, caused by a direct blow to the iliac crest, the top ridge of the pelvis. It is common in contact sports such as football. Recovery usually takes one to three weeks, according to Norton Healthcare. Giants QB J.J. McCarthy has one.. Giants QB J.J. McCarthy is expected to play Nov. 12, 2026, despite a hip pointer suffered against the Eagles.. Norton Healthcare says hip pointers often happen in contact sports but can also come from a fall. Symptoms include bruising, swelling and tenderness of the hip, limited range of motion and pain that can be severe and usually gets worse with activity. Doctors advise getting checked to rule out a more serious injury. Standard care is rest, ice and compression as soon as possible; anti-inflammatory or pain medication may help, and gentle stretching can ease stiffness. If pain lasts more than a couple of weeks, Norton recommends seeing a doctor again. Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the former Minnesota Vikings starter, hurt his hip in the Giants' win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported it was a hip pointer. Coach John Harbaugh said Monday that McCarthy was "doing well" and expected to play Thursday, Nov. 12, against the Washington Commanders.

What is Win the Mall on Netflix? The shopping competition, explained. Win the Mall is a Netflix reality competition premiering Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Ten teams of expert shoppers compete inside a real, working shopping mall to take control of storefronts, grow their spending power and outmaneuver rivals. Content creator Haley Baylee hosts, and Fremantle produces the series.. Netflix's new shopping competition Win the Mall premieres Nov. 18, 2026, just ahead of the Black Friday shopping season.. Netflix calls the show "the ultimate fantasy retail experience" that turns "a classic American shopping mall into a thrilling game of strategy and unexpected twists." The official logline describes it as "part shopping spree, part social strategy." Only one contestant is crowned the winner and walks away with what the producers call "the keys to the ultimate prize"; Netflix has not said what the prize is or which mall was used. Special guests Jonathan Van Ness, Keith Lee, Salish Matter and Lilly Singh join Baylee for mall-themed challenges. Baylee, whose name is sometimes misspelled "Haylee Baylee," is a former scientist who became a full-time creator, host and model; she won Sports Illustrated's Model Search in 2017. Netflix announced the series on March 17, 2026. Jimmy Fox executive produces for Fremantle, with Charles Wachter as showrunner.

What is CME FedWatch? A tool that tracks Fed rate cut and hike odds. CME FedWatch is a free tool run by the CME Group, a Chicago-based exchange operator, that shows the odds traders assign to changes in the Federal Reserve's benchmark interest rate. It turns prices from federal funds futures contracts into percentage probabilities for each upcoming Fed meeting. The tool is also written as CME Fed Watch.. The Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than the 0.3% economists expected. Market odds for the Fed's December decision moved after the release.. The tool breaks those odds down by meeting date and by the size of a move, such as no change, a quarter-point hike, or a half-point hike. Traders and reporters use it as a snapshot of market expectations, not as a forecast from the Fed itself. The next Fed meeting covered in current coverage is set for Dec. 8-9. On the day of the October consumer price report, the tool showed traders had fully priced in a quarter-point increase at that meeting, while the odds of a half-point increase stood at 13.6%. The Fed's benchmark rate was held in a range of 3.75% to 4% at its October meeting, when officials voted 10-2 to keep it there. The tool gained attention after the Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% that economists had expected. Stock futures slipped and Treasury yields rose after the release, a sign that markets moved toward expecting higher rates for longer. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said on Oct. 28 that the central bank wants price increases to ease.

What is the Anthropic IPO? Date, price range and valuation. The Anthropic IPO is the planned first public sale of shares in Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot. Anthropic will list on the Nasdaq in New York this month, November 2026, at $70 to $78 per share, valuing the company at about $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion.. Anthropic has set a price range of $70 to $78 per share for its stock market listing, valuing the company at up to about $1.3 trillion. The listing comes days after the US midterm elections, when AI-related stocks fell sharply.. Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion through the offering, according to the company's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The shares will trade under the ticker symbol "ANT." Earlier, some analysts had predicted a valuation near $2 trillion, so the announced range is lower than those estimates. The timing is sensitive. After the US midterm elections last week, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns that a Democrat-led Congress could slow AI development and the building of data centers. Global stocks also dropped as those fears spread to Asia and Europe. Anthropic's revenue rose to $16.2 billion in the first six months of 2026 from $1.1 billion a year earlier. Its valuation in a May 2026 funding round was $965 billion. Anthropic is based in San Francisco and was founded in January 2021 by former OpenAI members, led by Dario Amodei as chief executive and Daniela Amodei as president. The company's filing says it expects to list in November 2026.
